newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARES SEEN LOWER OR FLAT.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARES SEEN LOWER OR FLAT.

text.p: Singapore shares may range-trade or slip a little further during the rest of this week, but they are unlikely to rally much, dealers said on Thursday.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended at 1,875.38 points on Wednesday, down 18.08 and at its lowest level since August 1993.
The market has been hit by poor half-year results, turmoil on the region's currencies and a year-long local economic slowdown.
Many dealers think the index could hit 1,800 points before rallying, a view supported by some chart analysts. But other dealers say Singapore is beginning to look relatively cheap.
"I think it will drift sideways, moving plus or minus 20 or 30 points from here," said one dealer. "I don't think we will see 1,800 points on the STII soon."
U.S. markets fell overnight, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 32.52 points to 7,928.32.
